newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle leaves space station Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle leaves space station Mir.

text.p: The space shuttle Atlantis undocked from Russia's Mir space station late on Sunday, leaving behind U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger for a four-month stay in space.
The two spacecraft parted company at 9:15 p.m. EST (0215 GMT) as they soared through space, 240 miles (386 km) above central Russia.
"We have physical separation," shuttle commander Mike Baker told mission control as the shuttle's docking ring released its metallic grip on Mir.
Atlantis was to circle the sprawling space station twice at a distance of 400 feet (121 metres), before moving off into a new orbit.

The shuttle's departure ended five days of joint operations for the two crews. Atlantis, on its fifth visit to Mir, picked up NASA astronaut John Blaha, who had been in space since September and dropped off Linenger.
During his four-month mission to Mir, Linenger will perform more than 80 experiments and conduct a spacewalk, the first from Mir by an American.
The shuttle will return to the station in May to collect the 42-year-old astronaut and bring his replacement, Mike Foale.
The shuttle also brought water, food and other supplies to the Russian space outpost and was leaving with the results of scientific experiments and space station components in need of repair.

The Atlantis astronauts bid farewell to the crew of space station Mir early on Sunday. The three Mir crewmen waved goodbye as the hatch connecting Atlantis and Mir was swung shut at 7:38 a.m. EST (1238 GMT).
Blaha, just days from his return to Earth, said he was looking forward to being reunited with his family but he would miss the view of earth from space.

"It's just a real pleasure to look at our beautiful planet," he said. "I love working up here but ... my wife and I have been married for over 30 years and I didn't realise I would miss her as much as I did."
The shuttle and Mir crews staged a farewell for the television cameras about three hours before they said their actual goodbyes.

"Unfortunately, we are saying goodbye to the excellent Atlantis crew," Mir commander Valeri Korzun said during the ceremony, which was conducted almost entirely in Russian. "We wish them a safe landing."

"We are also saying goodbye to our colleague the American astronaut John Blaha," he said. "We have had problems, but despite everything and anything we have remained friends and we have completed our tasks."
Blaha thanked his cosmonaut crewmates for their hospitality and stressed the importance of NASA's cooperative efforts with Russia.
"This programme is not only important for space exploration, but also for the relationship between the countries," he said.
At the end of the ceremony, Linenger peeled off his shuttle shirt and playfully tossed it after the departing Atlantis crew.
"I don't need that anymore," he quipped as he pulled on a blue Russian space station uniform.

Atlantis was scheduled to return to earth at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre on Wednesday. But NASA officials were considering extending the flight by one day to complete a test of an experimental space treadmill.
